metadata.content:
KoreLumina Knowledge Operations reconstruction — full task status
Current branch: inspect/runtime-certified-main
Current pushed HEAD: 217d69b849b30e2f72f61a1c7cdabca0c7556b02 — refactor(knowledge): remove obsolete flow appearance tokens. GitHub verification confirms the commit removed only the obsolete capsuleFlow* appearance definitions from flagshipAppearance.ts.
Overall status
The Knowledge Operations UI reconstruction is now in the late-stage Lumina Design System extraction / normalization phase. The Production workspace family and Learning workspace family have undergone extensive migration away from local styling ownership toward shared Lumina primitives and compositions.
The operating contract remains unchanged: UI first, production-grade polish first, then reusable Lumina extraction, with runtime/backend wiring later. Executive Hero / Executive Ribbon composition has remained untouched throughout.
Shared Lumina foundation established
The current normalized visual foundation includes:


LuminaFlagshipPanel for primary glass panels.


LuminaFlagshipCard for nested premium cards and metric surfaces.


LuminaFlagshipSurface for subordinate/nested surfaces.


LuminaExecutiveTitleMetricsComposition for title/metrics rail alignment.


LuminaBalancedSplitPanelComposition for true 50/50 Production layouts.


Shared semantic badges and segmented-tab primitives.


Executive-derived glass/material contract standardized in LuminaFlagshipCard.


Workspace visual-standard governance documentation established.


The Executive-derived glass material is now the visual reference for reusable workspace surfaces, while the Executive source itself remains immutable.
Production workspaces
Production migration is substantially complete.

Canonical Knowledge and Canonical Review were aligned to the same balanced rail contract. Knowledge Graph toolbar metrics were also moved onto LuminaFlagshipCard.
Flow Engine status
The Knowledge Capsule Flow Engine has now gone through its full visual-normalization sequence.
Completed:


Outer shell migrated to LuminaFlagshipPanel.


Internal Flow header moved onto LuminaExecutiveTitleMetricsComposition.


Live manufacturing posture metric moved to LuminaFlagshipCard.


No-results state moved to LuminaFlagshipSurface.


Zone-specific legacy visual treatments removed.

Station focus treatment normalized.

Capsule light/glow intensity reduced.


Capsule hover lift fixed by moving transform ownership to the outer capsule button.


Station-count presentation normalized.


Remediation/validated branch wrappers moved to LuminaFlagshipSurface.


All obsolete capsuleFlow* appearance tokens removed from flagshipAppearance.ts.


The final Flow cleanup commit removed 95 lines of dead visual-token ownership, and GitHub confirms the deletion was isolated to those obsolete definitions.
Flow Engine legacy capsuleFlow* ownership is closed.
Workspace-level Knowledge header
The top Knowledge workspace header was also normalized after the Flow Engine work exposed a separate visual mismatch.
Completed:


KnowledgeWorkspaceHeader migrated from a custom flex layout to LuminaExecutiveTitleMetricsComposition.


Production / Learning mode controls were compacted.


Educational Posture / Runtime status card was resized to match the switcher width.


Right-side controls now stack vertically.


Workspace title region is now wrapped in LuminaFlagshipPanel, so the top Production Pipeline / Institutional Knowledge Production and Learning equivalents inherit the same Lumina glass contract.


The right-side control stack remains inside LuminaFlagshipCard.


This means both the layout composition and the glass/material ownership of the top workspace header are now coming from shared Lumina contracts.
Learning workspace status
The Learning side had already undergone extensive normalization before the latest Production work.

Local FlagshipCard, FlagshipPanel, LearningPanel, and learningAppearance.ts removed where obsolete


One known visual issue remains intentionally unresolved from earlier work: Canonical Knowledge nested title-color consistency. Attempts to force the nested title tone to visually match the bright cyan heading did not produce the expected rendering, and that work was explicitly deferred rather than guessed further.
Legacy cleanup status
Major legacy local ownership removed:


obsolete local FlagshipCard


obsolete local FlagshipPanel


obsolete LearningPanel


obsolete learningAppearance.ts


old cardHighlight


old iconBox


old local badge ownership


old segmented appearance tokens


all capsuleFlow* tokens


Some legacy flagshipAppearance ownership still exists outside the Flow Engine. It should not be deleted wholesale. Remaining consumers must be audited individually before any further deletion.
Current build / repository condition
From the latest local Terminal validation:


npm run build passed.


Runtime TypeScript build passed.


Builder Vite production build passed.


git diff --check passed.


No remaining capsuleFlow definitions or consumers were found before deletion.


Pre-push validation passed.


Push completed successfully.


Current pushed commit is 217d69b849b30e2f72f61a1c7cdabca0c7556b02.


GitHub independently verifies that pushed commit.
Architectural state
The reconstruction has moved beyond isolated visual repairs. A consistent reusable workspace system now exists:
Executive material → Lumina primitives → Lumina compositions → Knowledge workspace consumers
That direction is now established and should continue one-way. Local workspace styling should be removed only after a shared Lumina contract has taken ownership and all consumers have been verified.
The backend/runtime still remains intentionally downstream of the finalized UI contract.
What remains
The next phase should be a fresh full Knowledge Operations residual-ownership audit, not another speculative local edit. Specifically, inspect all remaining flagshipAppearance consumers and classify them into:


legitimate semantic/local state styling that should remain,


reusable visual ownership that should move into Lumina primitives/compositions,


dead tokens that can be safely removed.


After that, the next logical milestone is whichever remaining workspace has the highest residual local visual ownership. Do not begin backend wiring yet.
Current task completion assessment
Knowledge Operations visual reconstruction: advanced / near closure

Production workspace primitive migration: substantially complete

Flow Engine normalization: complete

Knowledge workspace top header normalization: complete

Learning primitive migration: substantially complete

Dead Flow token cleanup: complete

Executive source integrity: preserved

Runtime/backend wiring: intentionally not started as part of this UI-contract phase

Next required action: residual global Knowledge visual-ownership audit before declaring extraction complete.
